newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Some Zaire assembly members demand rebel talks.
newsitem.headline: Some Zaire assembly members demand rebel talks.

text.p: Opposition members of Zaire's transitional parliament banded together on Tuesday to win a vote calling for a new government, a ceasefire and peace talks with rebels advancing in the east, witnesses said.

But most supporters of ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko, who hold a majority in the assembly, boycotted the session and the vote fell far short of the three quarters majority needed under Zaire's transitional constitution to have any effect.
"We should avoid taking decisions that violate the constitution," said Kanga Boongo, one of the few Mobutu supporters who stayed for the debate.

The motion, debated by less than half of the assembly's 738 members, was sponsored by the radical opposition led by Etienne Tshisekedi. A majority of those assembly members present approved the motion by acclamation.
Earlier, assembly members spent five hours debating what the debate should be about.

Mobutu, who has spent most of his time in Europe since prostate cancer surgery there in August, is in hospital in Monaco. Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo is in Kenya for talks on the crisis in Central Africa.
